main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem} Let $E/\Q$ be an elliptic curve and let $q$ be any prime. If $s_q(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then $r(E)=a(E)=s_q(E)$, $\#\Sha(E/\Q)<\infty$, and, with $r=r(E)$, $\frac{L^{(r)}(E,1)}{r!}=\frac{\Omega_E\Reg_E\,\#\Sha(E/\Q)\prod_{\ell}c_\ell(E)}{\#E(\Q)_{\rm tors}^{2}}$. There are no additional hypotheses on reduction, rational torsion, isogenies, complex multiplication, or residual Galois representations. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: If for SOME prime q the q-power Selmer group of E/Q has Z_q-corank 0 or 1, then the algebraic rank, the analytic rank and that corank coincide, Sha is finite, and the full BSD leading-term formula holds exactly (all primes), with Omega_E the period over all of E(R) and Reg_E the Neron-Tate regulator of the full Mordell-Weil lattice.
main_statement.stronger_internal_statement: M1 Prop center:odd-valuations (10-center.tex:231-237) plus M3 Thm 1.1 (s_2<=1 follows from a(E)<=1 by GZK) give: the full BSD formula holds for EVERY E/Q of analytic rank <= 1. The Selmer-corank hypothesis is used only to reach analytic rank <= 1 via M2. This analytic-rank form is not stated as a headline but follows directly.

companion_statements.paraphrase: For every E/Q, every prime p, r in {0,1}: s_p(E)=r => a(E)=rank E(Q)=r and Sha(E/Q) finite. Application (Cor 10.x): for every prime l = 4,7,8 mod 9, X^3+Y^3=lZ^3 has rank 1 and finite Sha (Sylvester's cube-sum cases).

For every E/Q with s_2(E)<=1: rank = a(E) = s_2(E), Sha finite, Q_E in Q_{>0} and v_2(Q_E)=v_2(#Sha). No restriction on E[2] or reduction at 2. Cor 15.x: with 006/Smith, exact 2-part for density-one of twists.

previously_open_and_how_handled.summary: Before this family (as far as the cited literature and our searches show), the p-part of BSD in analytic rank 0/1 was known only under hypotheses on p and E: Skinner-Urban (rank 0; p>=3 good ordinary, E[p] irreducible + ramification), Zhang 2014 and JSW 2017 (rank 1; p>=5 or p>=3, good ordinary/supersingular, semistable, irreducible + ramification), Castella / CGLS 2022 (rank 1, odd good ordinary Eisenstein primes), Keller-Yin 2024 (Eisenstein, multiplicative and potentially good ordinary incl. some additive), BCS 2025 (p>3 good ordinary, irreducible, ramification hypothesis removed), Castella 2024 (multiplicative), BSTW 2024 (semistable supersingular p, rank 0/1, from search snippet), Rubin + Burungale-Flach (CM rank 0, all p), LTYZ 2025 (CM rank 1, p=2 good ordinary), and the dyadic twist-family results (Zhao, CLTZ 2015, CLZ 2020, Shu-Zhai 2021, Kriz-Li 2019). Full BSD was known only for specific curves (Grigorov-Jorza-Patrikis-Stein-Tarnita, Miller: 16714 of 16725 curves of conductor <5000 in rank <=1 [snippet]) and explicit families (BSTW, Wan; Banwait-Huang 2026 [snippet]). Bhargava-Skinner-Zhang give the RANK part for >=66.48% of curves, not the formula.

items.name: Isogeny invariance
items.label: classical:isogeny
items.statement: Suppose $A$ and $A'$ are isogenous elliptic curves over $\Q$ of analytic rank at most one. Then \[ \frac{Q_A}{\#\Sha(A/\Q)} =\frac{Q_{A'}}{\#\Sha(A'/\Q)}. \] In particular $X(A)=X(A')$. Over a number field, the corresponding analytic-to-arithmetic BSD ratio is likewise invariant under isogeny when the Tate--Shafarevich groups are finite. It is compatible with products and restriction of scalars.

items.name: Full-index discrepancy identity
items.label: classical:discrepancy-identity
items.statement: Assume $L(E/K,s)$ has a simple zero under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{classical:gross-zagier}. Then \begin{equation} \frac{Q_E}{\#\Sha(E/\Q)} \frac{Q_{E^D}}{\#\Sha(E^D/\Q)} =\frac{[E(K):\Z P_K]^2} {c_E^2\prod_\ell c_\ell(E)^2\,\#\Sha(E/K)}. \end{equation} The index on the right is the full group index, including torsion. Consequently, at any prime $p$, if \[ n_P=v_p\bigl([E(K)/E(K)_{\rm tors}:\Z\overline P_K]\bigr), \qquad \tau_g=v_p(\#E(K)_{\rm tors}), \] then \begin{equation} X_p(E)+X_p(E^D) =2(n_P+\tau_g)-2v_p(c_E) -2\sum_\ell v_p(c_\ell(E))-v_p(\#\Sha(E/K)). \end{equation}

Multiplying gamma by a commutator sigma=[g,g'] in ker(G->GL(V)) changes u(gamma) by -e(a(g),d(g'))+e(a(g'),d(g)) without changing any other prescribed data; hence the obstruction can be made nondegenerate (strict case of M2) or made to span all (alternating / augmented) matrices (M1).
for_: Non-analytic: neither the commutator-modified address nor the obstruction pairing appears in the goal or in any statement of L; the goal is a BSD identity.

Load-bearing in all three papers: it gives the length<=2 upper bound that drives M2's contradiction in the strict case (the case Skinner 2020 excluded by hypothesis), residual concentration at every odd p in M1 (replacing residual irreducibility/ramification hypotheses), the codimension-two spanning in M1 Sec 9, and nonzero tame heights in M1 Sec 5 / M3 Sec 6.
It is what makes a tame (p-unramified) deformation direction usable in place of an Iwasawa variable at p, which is how the uniform treatment of additive/supersingular/Eisenstein p is achieved.
The paper itself names 'the marked residual obstruction calculation' as a reusable part (M1 01:260).
against: The ingredients are classical: the cup-product primitive evaluated at Frobenius is a Mazur-Tate tame height / Bertolini-Darmon derived height; u restricted to the kernel is the Heisenberg (Massey-product) central extension cocycle, and choosing Frobenius in a Heisenberg extension by Chebotarev is standard in Massey-product and Ramakrishna-type lifting arguments.
Choosing auxiliary primes with prescribed Frobenius to kill Selmer/obstruction classes is the Ramakrishna / Taylor-Wiles / Kolyvagin-prime pattern.
Only one quick search was run; an expert may identify the exact device in Zhang's level-raising or in Sweeting's bipartite Euler system arguments.

checked: Assembly logic M1 10:254-270: correct given its inputs (positive rational with all v_p = 0 equals 1).

Discrepancy identity M1 02:261-318: restriction of scalars Res_{K/Q}E ~ E x E^D, period A_E/sqrt(d_K), component product prod c_l^2 (bad primes split), regulator 2H_abs(P_0): consistent with JSW/Zhang-style computations.

Exact center M1 10:34-141: valuation bookkeeping (Kummer volume 2n_P+2tau_g-s_K, local corrections, Haar identities) is internally consistent; cancellation of 2h is legitimate since log_omega P_K != 0.

Unit argument M1 09: logic (horizontal divisor of enlarged quotient -> theta implication -> simultaneous jump at a height-one prime of S_(f,y) -> contradiction with codim>=2) is coherent; the step 'F in (f,y) so (F) survives as a height-one prime of S_(f,y)' is fine.
M2 Lemma base-green: Poitou-Tate argument correct; the skew-symmetric graph plus c-equivariance forcing u=0 is correct for p odd.

M2 Lemma nonzero-obstruction: the Heisenberg identity u([g,g']) = -e(a(g),d(g'))+e(a(g'),d(g)) on N_V (where eps=1) is correct; joint span of (a,d^-) on N_V uses irreducibility and End=Q_p (needs absolute irreducibility of V over K and L, which is argued from open image / CM-field exclusion).
M2 Prop green-length: devissage along t is correct given the obstruction lemma.
concerns: Ultralimit framework (EC2): the 'Galois group' is replaced by sequences of Galois elements modulo an ultrafilter; admissible cohomology is shown to agree with H^1(G_{K,S},V) at t=0 (M2 lem:admissible-specialization), but all deformation-theoretic statements in t and the transfer of theta/automorphic congruences to this limiting object need expert checking. M1 Lemma models:finite-models asserts uniform bounds on residual cohomology with growing ramification at moving primes from a two-sentence argument (03:121-129).

Extreme compression: proofs of deep steps (cusp lifting on U(3,1) PEL compactifications, Galois-side Hodge-Newton contacts, uniform nilpotent control, theta position-cut moment bounds) are a few paragraphs each; several proofs say 'the usual', 'for completeness', 'as in [C]'.

Dependency on unreviewed model-produced inputs: 006 (2-converse and twist density; itself relies on Smith 2025 preprint) is essential to M1 and M2; M1 cites M2 lemma-by-lemma (e.g. [C, Lemma 8.6], [C, Prop 9.7]), so an error in M2 propagates. The 2-converse is proved twice (006 and M3), which is a useful redundancy check but also unreviewed twice.

M2 relies on very recent human preprints for inputs (BHTY 2026, Burungale-Tian 2026 Annals rank-0 p-converse for context only) and on Labesse's base change with a sign property verified in-house (08:100-130).

M2 appendix (10-nonstandard-transfer.tex, 484 lines) proves statements about nonstandard weighted orbital integrals citing an undated author draft (Halleck-Dube) with a SHA-256 hash, but no proof in M2 references the appendix and Sec 8 explicitly says Labesse's argument 'does not use the weighted fundamental lemma' (08:51-55). Likely a leftover from an earlier route; harmless but a sign of incomplete editing.

M1 Oct-3 edition cited \cite{B,C,Dv} with no bibitem Dv; history.md says the citation was to 'a removed supporting manuscript'. A supporting manuscript was apparently removed from the release before publication; its content and whether any argument silently depended on it is unknown.

Scope subtlety: the headline is stated for Selmer corank, but the odd-p and 2-part arguments are proved for analytic rank <=1; the Selmer hypothesis enters only through M2. If M2 failed, M1 would still claim full BSD in analytic rank <=1 (given M3 and 006 for auxiliary fields).
CM rank-one curves at odd p are handled only through the pair identity with a CM rank-zero twist (Burungale-Flach); the non-maximal-order reduction (10:187-198) is brief.

extraction_friction: No Lean; all items from LaTeX.

Three manuscripts reuse the same lemma names (finite models, line switch, square switch, Kummer volume, series division, residual concentration) with different proofs at p odd vs p=2; items are kept separate per manuscript.

Core devices are introduced in prose or display math without environments: the tame variables u_j (M1 04:43-56), psi=(1+t)^ell (M2 03:255-268), U_w=B_w/L_w (M1 01:197-203), the Heisenberg commutator step (inside proofs: M2 03:560-600, M1 09:330-345, M3 06:210-224). A naive extractor misses them.
Cross-paper citations by lemma number into PDFs of companion papers ([C, Lemma 8.6]) make the DAG span manuscripts.
Labels in M1 equations are renamed 'eq:source-N' (numbered 1-24), suggesting machine post-processing.
M2 has an unused appendix; M3 Sec 13 proofs are written in dense run-on paragraphs (e.g. 13:1053-1101).
